# fortiappseccloud_waf_template_rewriting_requests

Configures rewriting requests for one FortiAppSec Cloud WAF template using the static template endpoint `/waf/template/{template_id}/rewriting_requests`. This resource owns the template's module settings. To make an application inherit them, configure the matching app module resource with `template = true` and omit its `configs` block.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_rewriting_requests` resource for a WAF template.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_template_rewriting_requests" "example" {
  template_id = fortiappseccloud_waf_template.example.template_id

  configs {
    status               = true
    x_forwarded_for      = true
    identify_original_ip = true
    x_header             = "X-Forwarded-For"

    rule_list {
      item {
        name                = "rewrite-example"
        action              = "rewrite-header-advanced"
        host_filter         = true
        host_expression     = "^(example\\.com)$"
        header_status       = true
        insert_header_name  = "X-Terraform-Matrix"
        insert_header_value = "enabled"

        remove_header {
          item {
            header = "X-Old-Header"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

- `template_id` (Required, Forces replacement) — WAF template ID.
- `configs` (Required) — Typed rewriting requests configuration. Its attributes and ownership-wrapper blocks are identical to `fortiappseccloud_waf_rewriting_requests` when that app resource uses `template = false`.

## Import

Import using the template ID:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_template_rewriting_requests.example TEMPLATE_ID
```

The first read after import hydrates all supported ownership wrappers.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
